https://www.barrons.com/articles/google-and-apple-are-still-cheap-microsoft-not-so-much-1515165962 Google and Apple Are Still Cheap. Microsoft, Not So Much By Updated Jan. 5, 2018 10:26 a.m. ET Text Size Medium Large 
Tech had a great year in 2017, outperforming all other sectors, and mega caps like the Fang stocks ( Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ), and Alphabet/Google ( GOOGL )) saw big gains as well. Yet even with 2017's massive rally, tech giant shares still look cheap, argues MKM Partners' Rob Sanderson . Illustration: Bloomberg News 
Sanderson writes that in general, the relative valuation of mega-cap tech stocks, including Fang stocks and Apple ( AAPL ), relative to the S&P 500 increased in the third quarter, but then decreased in the fourth quarter, as value significantly outperformed growth toward the end of the year 
While year-end premiums for big tech were still higher at the end of the fourth quarter than at mid-year, Sanderson highlights that relative valuation is still "well below" the five- and ten-year historic averages. 
However, there's been a bifurcation, he writes, with the consumer tech giants still looking cheap, while IT firms have been bid up: Examining a cohort of mega-cap enterprise technology suppliers (including Microsoft ( MSFT ), Oracle ( ORCL ) and SAP ( SAP )) exemplifies a rotation to more conservative tech exposure over the past several quarters. Compared to its five-year average, valuation of MSFT is significantly above recent history. Similar for SAP, which has seen its premium to the market multiple expand through the year, hitting 5-year highs in Q4. The discount that ORCL has typically traded to the market had gotten to 5-year lows before the significant correction in December and is now about 1-point lower than the 5-year average. 
The Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF ( XLK ) is up 0.7% to $66.07 this morning. Most Popular
